belief: We don't talk about our problems outside the family.
origins: Many families, cultures, and churches prize privacy. Some of that is wise: not every struggle belongs on social media. But when the rule hardens into “never tell anyone,” abuse, addiction, depression, and money trouble can go unaddressed for years. Children learn to keep secrets, and adults carry hurts alone because speaking up feels like betrayal.
teaches: Scripture honors both discretion and honesty. Paul writes, “Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” James says, “Confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed.” Proverbs says, “He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.” And “Open your mouth for those with no voice.” Wisdom chooses whom to tell and how, but secrecy that keeps people suffering or in danger is not what God asks of a family.
self_statements: What happens at home stays at home.
Talking about it would shame us.
If I tell, I am betraying them.
We just do not speak about that.
errors: Believing I must tell everyone or no one.
Insisting that I should never share family struggles.
Imagining that telling anyone will destroy the family.
Feeling disloyal and concluding that I am.
questions: Where did I learn this rule, and what was it meant to protect?
What has silence cost me and my family?
Who is a wise, trustworthy person I could talk with?
What is the difference between privacy and secrecy?
Is anyone in danger because we are keeping quiet?
What does Scripture say about bearing burdens together?
truth: Healthy privacy is wise, but silence that keeps people hurting is not. I can share my burdens with trustworthy people, seek help for my family, and still honor those I love. If anyone is in danger, speaking up is the loving thing to do.
hw_truths: We are meant to carry burdens together.
Confession and prayer lead to healing.
Privacy and secrecy are not the same.
Speaking up can be an act of love.
I can choose wise, safe people.
log: Each week, note one honest conversation with a safe person and what you learned.
actions: Write the unspoken rule and who taught it.
Choose a pastor, counselor, or trusted friend.
Tell them part of the story and see how it goes.
Get help if anyone is unsafe.
If someone is in danger, call 911 or the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.
prayer: Lord, my family taught me to keep quiet. Give me wisdom about whom to trust, courage to speak, and healing as I carry burdens with others. Protect those I love. Amen.
hw_questions: What is the rule in my family?
What is privacy and what is secrecy?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can carry burdens with others and still honor my family.”
